slot.subtopic: Active to Passive Voice – present perfect/continuous tenses
slot.brief: Ask the student to pick the correct passive transformation of a present perfect sentence (e.g., 'has completed'); distractors with wrong auxiliary or participle forms.

stem: Change the voice: The research team has submitted the final report to the director.
options: The final report has been submitted to the director by the research team.
The final report have been submitted to the director by the research team.
The final report has submitted to the director by the research team.
The final report had been submitted to the director by the research team.

verdicts.working: Present perfect active (“has submitted”) becomes present perfect passive (“has been submitted”).

working:
Present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle. “Report” is singular, so use “has been submitted.”

Independent check: Present perfect active (“has submitted”) becomes present perfect passive (“has been submitted”).
solution: Present perfect active changes to passive as $has/have + been + past participle$. Since “report” is singular, the passive form is “has been submitted.”

draft.working: Present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle. “Report” is singular, so use “has been submitted.”
draft.distractor_notes: B uses a plural auxiliary with a singular subject. C omits “been” and leaves the active-form verb. D changes the tense to past perfect.
